name: Swell-sensing battery pack
subtitle: a battery pack that feels a cell bulging

effects.effect: pressure on a confined liquid is passed on equally everywhere

effect: pressure on a confined liquid is passed on equally everywhere
how: Lithium cells often swell for hours or days before they catch fire, but a car or home battery holds hundreds of cells and a sensor on each costs too much. Thin, linked fluid pockets sit between the cells; a cell bulging anywhere squeezes them, the pressure spreads through all the pockets alike (Pascal's law), and one gauge tells the pack to shut down.
obstacle: Cells also swell harmlessly as they charge and warm up, so the alarm must tell normal breathing from danger.
why: Battery fires in cars, homes and e-bikes are rising; an early, cheap warning saves lives.
real: Battery swelling is detected with per-cell pressure/force or resistance sensors between cells; no design using linked fluid pockets feeding one gauge was found.
